★★★ D-ASM-EXTERNAL-CALL-UNREPRESENTABLE — A `.s` MAY CALL OUT OF ITS TRANSLATION UNIT. Before this row `call putchar` was refused by name: `AsmTextModule` carried no extern, so every call had to resolve to a function defined in the same file, which is not what assembly is for.

★★★ HOW A `.s` DECLARES AN EXTERN: IT DOESN'T, AND THAT IS THE SPEC. gas has no extern directive — its `.extern` is documented as accepted and IGNORED ("as treats all undefined symbols as external") — so a symbol referenced by a call and defined nowhere in the file simply IS one. Requiring a directive would refuse assembly that every reference assembler accepts, which [[feedback_reference_compilers_are_the_spec]] treats as the same class of defect as accepting what none accept.

★★ ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 AGAINST GNU as ITSELF, which is the only check that settles it. Both toolchains were given this file's `call` shape and both emitted: symbol `puts`/`putchar` as `NOTYPE GLOBAL DEFAULT UND` in `.symtab`, and one `R_X86_64_PLT32` relocation per call site at the displacement. Same binding, same type, same relocation kind — DSS's object is not merely 'valid', it is the one gas produces.

★★ WHY `libraryPath` IS EMPTY ON THE IMPORT ROW, stated here because it is the decision the row rests on. A `.s` names no owning image. Filling one in from the dialect would make the LANGUAGE a second owner of a fact the descriptor corpus owns — which is precisely the split-CRT defect UCRT-P4 deleted from the C path by REMOVING the per-language library default rather than repointing it. An unbound import is exactly what a C bare prototype produces, so the linker's existing three-flavor reference gate judges both by one implementation.

★★★ AND THAT GATE IS WHY THIS ROW HAS THE ARMS IT HAS — each is a DIFFERENT verdict from that one policy, not three spellings of one:
  • RELOCATABLE `.o` / `.obj` — a later (foreign) linker resolves the undefined symbol. KEPT, and the object carries it.
  • ELF `.so` (ET_DYN) — `ld -shared` semantics: ld.so resolves it from the loading process's global scope. KEPT; ✔MEASURED, the emitted `.so` carries `putchar` as `UND` in `.dynsym` beside its own exported `main`, and emits no DT_NEEDED (correct — a `-shared` link does not name libc either).
  • EXEC image — nothing binds later, so the reference is REFUSED LOUD. That arm is its own example (`asm_x86_64_extern_call_exec_unbound_error`), because a manifest is either an expect-error one or a build one.

$exitCodeComment: REQUIRED BY THE MANIFEST SCHEMA, ASSERTED BY NOTHING. The harness demands an integer `exitCode` on every non-expect-error manifest, and every arm here is `runOn: []`, so the value is never compared against anything. It is 0 because that is what `main` returns; read it as documentation of the source, not as a pin.
